# Open sourced for all to use

# AlphaChip: An open-source framework for generating chip floorplans with distributed deep reinforcement learning.

AlphaChip is an open-source framework for generating chip floorplans with distributed deep reinforcement learning. This framework reproduces the methodology published in the Nature 2021 paper:

A graph placement methodology for fast chip design. Azalia Mirhoseini, Anna Goldie, Mustafa Yazgan, Joe Wenjie Jiang, Ebrahim Songhori, Shen Wang, Young-Joon Lee, Eric Johnson, Omkar Pathak, Azade Nazi, Jiwoo Pak, Andy Tong, Kavya Srinivasa, William Hang, Emre Tuncer, Quoc V. Le, James Laudon, Richard Ho, Roger Carpenter & Jeff Dean, 2021. Nature, 594(7862), pp.207-212. [PDF]

AlphaChip--one of the first reinforcement learning approaches used to solve a real-world engineering problem has led to a proliferation of research in AI for chips over the past few years. It is now used to design layouts for chips across Alphabet and outside, and has been extended to various stages of the design process, including logic synthesis, macro selection, timing optimization, and more! We hope that researchers will continue building on top of AlphaChip methodologies and open-source framework. Please see our blogpost for more information.

AlphaChip is built on top of TF-Agents and TensorFlow 2.x with support for eager execution, distributed training across multiple GPUs, and distributed data collection scaling to 100s of actors.

## Benefits of ML-Based Place & Route

Allow ASIC designers to quickly generate many alternatives with different tradeoffs of area, timing, etc.

Quickly re-do layout even if major changes in design upstream (very helpful for full automated design space exploration upstream)

Can significantly reduce time/effort needed to develop new ASICs

Can give pretty good QoR estimates in ~1 sec: critical for rapid exploration of higher-level architecture choices and synthesis decisions

## The FAST Datapath Search Space

- Goal: create an approximate superset template capable of describing scalar, vector, and matrix processors with a flexible memory hierarchy

Scalar/vector units are described by setting systolic array dimensions to 1

Memory levels are optional and can be private or shared

## FAST Search Results Performance-per-TDP vs TPUv3

Perf/TDP measures of performance / power (important in datacenters)

- EfficientNet-B0...B7 are different sizes of vision models

Green bars are for customizing accelerator to a particular single model

Perf/TDP improvements of ~3X to ~6X

“TPU-v3” here is hypothetical TPU-v3 die-shrunk to same sub-10-nm process

## Application-Specific Integrated Circuits

Being able to easily customize and optimize for specific workloads instead of building a more general purpose device can lead to significant improvements

## Application-Specific Integrated Circuits

## Being able to easily customize and optimize for specific workloads instead of building a more general purpose device can lead to significant improvements

If we can truly drive down the time and investment required to build a custom chip by 20-100X, we will see an amazing proliferation of customized & more efficient chips for ever-more specialized applications

## Summary

Use learned algorithms, that can generalize from their own RL experience and learn from other designs, etc.

Make fast reward functions that can take into account downstream effects

Use massively parallel search+learning in order to effectively explore the space of decisions

With the right end-to-end approaches, automated or mostly-automated design of entire chips should be possible
